extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of nature/lyrical essays; students of descriptive prose and creative nonfiction
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting descriptive, reflective prose about natural places that blends precise observation, anecdote, and philosophical insight in a lyrical voice. Emphasizes sensory detail, temporal depth, and metaphor to connect landscape and inner thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific, quantitative detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Use precise measurements and concrete particulars (distances, depths, acreages, temperatures) to ground description in verifiable fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: 'half a mile long and a mile and three quarters in circumference, and contains about sixty-one and a half acres'; 'the bottom can easily be discerned at the depth of twenty-five or thirty feet'; thermometer readings and fish weights. Such specificity lends verisimilitude and anchors lyrical reflection; include numbers, named places, and precise observations rather than vague generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary perspective by distance and angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent how an object changes with viewpoint: distant appearance versus close-up appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoreau: 'All our Concord waters have two colors at least; one when viewed at a distance, and another, more proper, close at hand.' Use contrasts of near/far, hill-top versus boat, looking down versus looking across to capture multifaceted appearance and the role of light and angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained central metaphor linking landscape and inner life
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a controlling metaphor that ties the physical feature to human experience or psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by: 'A lake is the landscape's most beautiful and expressive feature. It is earth's eye; looking into which the beholder measures the depth of his own nature.' Use a fresh, coherent metaphor (eye, mirror, etc.) and return to it to unify description and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise natural-history and taxonomic detail for authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Name species, behaviors, and natural-history particulars to convey knowledge and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: species names and identifications ('white-bellied swallows (Hirundo bicolor)', 'peetweets (Totanus macularius)', 'Leuciscus pulchellus'), fish types, and behavioral notes. Such details enrich texture and suggest close observation; avoid generic 'birds'/'fish' when a specific name will do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground universal reflection in anecdote and mundane incident
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor philosophical or lyrical claims in concrete episodes, small anecdotes, or everyday actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoreau uses moments like retrieving an axe through the ice, midnight fishing, or boiling chowder on a sand-bar to segue into larger meditations. Use short narrated scenes to justify or illustrate abstractions—show how the thought arises from lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evocative simile and cross-sensory metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor vivid similes and metaphors that blend sensory domains to create strong images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'like molten glass cooled but not congealed', 'the fluviatile trees... are the slender eyelashes which fringe it'. Use comparisons that illuminate rather than cliché; cross-sensory metaphors (sight as touch, sound as texture) are effective here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to subtle light and color shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe nuanced color changes and lighting effects across times and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages note how Walden appears blue or green depending on weather, angle, and depth; glass held to light is colorless though the pond appears green from mass. Track how color varies with season, depth, sky, and agitation of water to convey living perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal depth and seasonality
rubrics_metrics.description: Convey long-term change and seasonal cycles to situate place in time and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoreau documents rises and falls over years, spring thaw canals, seasonal insect presence, and historical changes in surrounding woods. Use observations spanning seasons and years to show continuity and change, rather than frozen snapshots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of scale and tonal appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Match the scope and tone of description to the scale of the scene—prefer humble, attentive description for modest landscapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'The scenery of Walden is on a humble scale'—avoid unwarranted grandeur; allow the small-scale scene to carry weight through careful detail and attention rather than hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of contrast and paradox to reveal complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ surprising juxtapositions and apparent contradictions to deepen understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: water that appears green yet a glass is colorless; a pond both pure and subject to seasonal muddiness; the same water at once young and ancient. Use contrasts to complicate simple readings and invite reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythmic, musical diction and sentence cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft sentences with attention to sound, repetition, and rhythm to produce lyrical prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text uses hummed psalms, repeated phrasings, balanced clauses, and onomatopoeia ('hissing') to create music. Vary sentence length, employ parallelism and alliteration where appropriate to make prose sing without sacrificing clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate local lore and human history
rubrics_metrics.description: Weave myths, place-names, and local anecdotes into the natural description to enrich cultural resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoreau includes Indian fable about Walden's naming, the old log canoe, and villagers' memories. Such elements situate the landscape in human time and make the place layered and storied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend moral/political asides judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow environmental description to host pointed social critique or moral observation when it arises naturally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: invective against the 'devilish Iron Horse' (railroad) that has 'browsed off' the woods. Use such commentary sparingly and rooted in the scene so it feels integral, not sermonizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit uncertainty and preserve curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limits of knowledge and show inquiry rather than dogma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoreau confesses not having proved certain hypotheses ('How large a body of Walden water would be required to reflect a green tint I have never proved'). Such humility keeps the narrator curious and credible; include open questions and provisional statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show rather than abstractly tell using small causal details
rubrics_metrics.description: Report small causal chains and sensory evidence (ripples, insect behavior, fish dimples) to let the reader infer larger truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages detail how a fish's leap produces ripples visible far away, or how skaters disappear with frost. Use concrete cause-effect scenes rather than declarative summaries to let scenes demonstrate claims.
